_note:
P4's OTHER half: the five tools whose turn ends by ASKING THE USER IN PROSE with no card at all — 'would you like me to...' — measured at 45 runs with zero errors and called 0/5.

A single-turn fixture cannot answer that question, so whether the model would ACT on a yes was never measured, and 'called 0/5' could not mean what the report said it meant. The added turn is the plainest possible answer, and it is what a real author would type.

ONLY `follow_ups`, `approve` and `max_approvals` change; the measured prompt and every seed and falsifier carry over unedited. fe_runner measures the LAST turn, so the tool must be called in response to the confirmation rather than in the opening turn.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: still called 0/5 after an explicit yes. Then the model is not waiting for permission and the prose-question reading is wrong — recorded per tool, not explained away.

scenarios.prompt: Apply arc template — use one of my library arc templates on this book.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM structure_node WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND kind='arc'
seed_assert.why: ZERO arcs before, so an applied template is attributable — and, the card never being approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: an arc is materialised with NO confirm card, OR the model invents an arc_template_id rather than listing the library first (composition_arc_template_list is the supplier). CONTROL: the account genuinely holds arc templates, so 'there are none' would contradict a known reading and is a finding either way.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; applying a template materialises structure.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an arc_template_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — book-scoped, and the template library is account-scoped: another account's template must not apply.

follow_ups: Yes, go ahead and do it.

scenarios.prompt: Update the divergence spec for my derivative — archive derivative if it is stale.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM composition_work WHERE source_work_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: NO derivative exists, and one cannot be seeded: composition_create_derivative is confirm-gated and its card is never approved in this loop, precisely because deriving is 'only archivable (not undoable)'. So this is a PRECONDITION CHAIN by construction, and a refusal naming the missing derivative is the correct outcome.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the model invents a project_id for a derivative that does not exist, OR the reply claims a divergence spec was updated or a derivative archived when there is none, OR it picks `archive` on a prompt whose primary verb is update — the prompt deliberately names both so the CHOICE is observable, and archiving something the author only asked to update would be acting beyond the request.

ship_audit.absent_case: This scenario IS the absent case — no derivative exists.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — another account's derivative must not be editable or archivable.

follow_ups: Yes, go ahead and do it.

scenarios.prompt: Adopt motif — copy one of the built-in tropes into my library so I can customise it.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['adopt motif'] + ['copy trope to my library'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE status='active' AND owner_user_id IS NULL
seed_assert.why:
EIGHTY-FOUR system/unlisted motifs already exist, so there is genuinely something to adopt and the model must FIND one — composition_motif_book_list / a motif search is the supplier. Read from the store rather than assumed. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with batch 15's arc templates: the system arc-template library is EMPTY, so this is the first tool in the loop whose cross-tenancy source actually has rows.

🔴 status='active' ADDED 2026-08-23 by the lifecycle-predicate gate. The tool reads active rows only (get_by_codes filters status='active'), so without this the assertion could pass over rows the tool is structurally unable to see — which is exactly what happened to composition_motif_link_edit for fifteen runs. Verified NOT to change the seeded value: all 84 system motifs are active today, so this tightens the assertion without moving its number.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif WHERE owner_user_id='019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c' AND code LIKE 'adopted-%'
seed_assert.why: SCOPED, not a headcount of the caller's library. That library is 152 and MOVING — the other scenarios in this batch seed into it, and my own seed-smoke added a row while I was verifying the fixture. The system side (84, owner_user_id NULL) is stable and is asserted above; here the check is simply that no ADOPTED clone exists yet, so one appearing is attributable to this turn.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a clone lands with NO confirm card (Tier W — its own description says adopting 'crosses the tenancy boundary and counts against your library quota', which is why it is human-confirmed), OR the model invents a motif_id rather than listing the built-ins first, OR it passes retag_genres the author never mentioned — retagging is optional and silently re-genre-ing an adopted motif changes what it will match later.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit — this is a cross-tenancy copy against a quota.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a motif_id that is neither public nor the caller's must be refused.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — 🔴 THIS TOOL CROSSES THE BOUNDARY BY DESIGN, so the check is the inverse of every other one in this batch: adopting a PUBLIC motif must be allowed, and adopting another USER's private motif must not.

follow_ups: Yes, go ahead and do it.

scenarios.prompt: What background jobs do I have running?
follow_ups: Yes, go ahead and do it.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is jobs_list's own purpose; the MEASURED turn is jobs_cancel's synonyms ['stop job'] + ['stop a running job'], verbatim. Two turns because service AND job_id are both required and jobs_list is their only supplier.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'pending', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: A PENDING translation job on the throwaway book. Seeded in SQL because the only tool that starts one is translation_start_job, which SPENDS, and a cost-bearing card is never approved. ONE row in ONE statement — batch 36's multi-row seed gave two rows the same created_at and collided with the startup migration's ROW_NUMBER renumber, taking the service into a restart loop.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND status='pending'
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE pending job — the SELECT that proves the SQL seed did what it claims. `pending` is what makes a cancel meaningful; a terminal job would make any answer look right. The card is never approved, so the status must still be 'pending' afterwards, and 'cancelled' would mean the cancel landed unapproved.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is cancelled with NO confirm card, OR the model invents a job_id rather than reading one from turn 1, OR it passes the wrong `service` — the tool takes service + job_id as a PAIR, so a right id under the wrong service either misses or, worse, reaches a different service's job with a colliding id. CONTROL FROM THE DESCRIPTION: cancel is 'free and reversible-by-restart — no spend, no confirm', so a reply warning the author that cancelling will cost them, or that the work cannot be recovered, is wrong about its own tool in the direction that would stop a safe action.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the description says no confirm, so what the card actually does is the thing to record.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a job_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — cancelling an already-cancelled job must refuse or be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — the description says the CALLER'S OWN jobs; another account's job_id must be refused.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'pending', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: The same single-statement pending job. PAUSE and CANCEL are near-neighbours with adjacent synonyms, which is exactly why each of these two scenarios names the other as its wrong-tool failure.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND status='pending'
seed_assert.why: ONE pending job. The card is never approved, so it must still be 'pending' — neither 'paused' nor 'cancelled'.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is paused with NO confirm card, OR the model reaches for `jobs_cancel` instead — cancel is terminal and pause is not, so cancelling a job the author asked to hold destroys work they meant to resume, and the two tools' synonym sets sit right beside each other — OR it invents a job_id. CONTROL: pause 'stops dispatching new units + drains in-flight; resume later from the GUI', so a reply promising to resume it automatically, or offering a resume tool, is describing something this tool does not provide.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the description says no confirm.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a job_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — pausing an already-paused job must be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — the CALLER'S OWN jobs only.
